newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina says mulling Brazil car reprisals.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says mulling Brazil car reprisals.

text.p: Argentina may seek to exclude cars produced at a new Brazilian factory from the benefits of the Mercosur customs union, Argentine Industry Secretary Alieto Gaudagni said Thursday.
Argentina's main car industry lobby, ADEFA, has called on the government to refuse to recognize as Mercosur products cars produced at a factory to be built by South Korea's Asia Motors Co Ltd.
Asked about the government's response, Guadagni said: "We are not ruling out any possibility," according to the state-run Telam news agency.
Brazil last week launched a program of incentives to attract investments in the north, northeast and west of Brazil including big cuts in tariffs for importing car parts.
Immediately after the Brazilian move, Asia Motors announced it was investing $500 million to install a factory to build passenger vehicles.
Guadagni said he will explain Argentina's position on the subject to Brazilian Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles in the second week of January.
"We want the first person to hear our proposals to be Minister Dornelles," Guadagni said.
An Industry Secretary spokesman told Reuters he could give no details of what action Argentina was planning to take.
The Mercosur customs union groups Argentina and Brazil with Uruguay and Paraguay. Chile and Bolivia recently agreed free trade pacts with the bloc.
